A burst of concurrent authenticated requests can occupy the entire bounded worker pool during a blip. Epistemic status upgraded to verified in Gate 4 (see G11-UP-PERF-VERIFY) with real measured numbers 2-3x worse than this finding's own initial framing.

Joint effect: after f8bbb06db, no RBAC configuration is immune to a PG degrade converting per-request authorization into blocking PG attempts.
classification_rationale: Read directly. Same root cause as G11-PERF-A, one fix (fail-fast circuit breaker) closes both. Do NOT revert f8bbb06db — it correctly closes a real HIGH security gap; this finding is about its unreviewed performance side effect.

trigger: same trigger as G11-PERF-A/B, now measured not reasoned: a saturated (not down) Postgres pool during check_permission/check_scoped_permission calls
summary: Empirical upgrade of G11-PERF-A/B from likely to verified. Measured (starved size-1 pool, live PG, 2 identical runs): single check_permission=4000ms (2x kReadTimeout — maybe_refresh_generation's own acquire stacks in front of check_permission's own acquire, not 1x as originally framed); warm-cache-then-degrade=4000ms identical to cold (cache gives zero protection once degraded); check_scoped_permission=6000ms (3x kReadTimeout, resolve_perm_groups stacks a third acquire); N=8 concurrent=4000ms total wall-clock with PgPool::waiters()=8 sampled mid-run, confirming PARALLEL worker-pool pinning not serialization. Worse than G11-PERF-A's own 'up to kReadTimeout=2s' framing by 2-3x. Fleet-scale full-HTTP-outage arithmetic (>=264 default / >=10 hand-pinned-floor concurrent requests during the window) remains likely, not load-tested end-to-end.
classification_rationale: Live measurement, test diff and raw output preserved at /tmp scratchpad (session-scoped, not committed). Methodology: extended f8bbb06db's own starved-pool construction, ran twice, identical numbers both times.

trigger: an operator/orchestrator issues SIGTERM (or otherwise calls stop()) while Postgres is saturated/slow AND the HTTP worker pool has in-flight/queued requests hitting check_permission/check_scoped_permission
summary: server.cpp's stop() calls web_server_->stop() then web_thread_.join() with NO deadline; httplib's ThreadPool::worker() drains every already-queued job before honoring shutdown_. Under this round's measured 4-6s per authz-touching request, a backlog queued during a sustained degrade multiplies shutdown latency with no bound — contrast the adjacent gRPC surface, which already has an explicit 5s Shutdown(deadline). Pre-existing shutdown machinery (httplib/server.cpp stop() sequencing predates #2703) was benign under the old near-instant SQLite RbacStore; this PR's multi-second blocking behavior is what turns it into a hazard. No memory-safety defect — store-teardown ordering (rbac_store_.reset() before pg_pool_.reset()) is confirmed correct and cannot race an in-flight worker.
classification_rationale: Code-path verified directly against vendored httplib.h and server.cpp; not live full-stack tested (no actual SIGTERM sent to a running ServerImpl this round).

Degraded (double-table-locked, 20 concurrent requests, statement_timeout=30s active as an external escape valve): 30.77s (+20.68s delta, individual denied-request latencies staircased 6-30s). Degraded with a genuinely frozen (docker-paused) Postgres, no statement_timeout escape valve: server STILL ALIVE at +90s post-SIGTERM with no sign of returning -- confirmed unbounded, not just slow.
classification_rationale: Live empirical reproduction, 3 configurations, real yuzu-server binary + real Postgres containers, all infrastructure torn down after. Chaos-injector recommends BLOCKING pending exact I-band adjudication.

With pool saturated (postgres-pool-size=4, http-worker-threads=10, the practical CLI floor) and 20 concurrent RBAC-gated requests in flight, GET /livez (zero-auth, zero-DB-touch health-probe route) went from 0.5ms baseline to 5.95-9.0s -- over 10,000x slowdown -- confirming the shared worker pool starves ALL routes including liveness probes, not just RBAC-gated ones. Compounding cross-finding risk noted: an orchestrator liveness-probe timeout during a degrade could trigger a restart, which then hits G11-CHAOS-SHUTDOWN-VERIFY's unbounded-join issue -- a plausible restart-loop/stuck-terminating-pod cascade.
classification_rationale: Live empirical reproduction against a real booted server. Chaos-injector recommends BLOCKING pending exact I-band adjudication.
